diagram_semantics: Individual arrows show conditional workflow stages or data dependencies, not an exhaustive literal call graph or observed runtime stack. Read the caption and source of each node. Overview edges are explicitly labelled. A method existing in source does not establish ordinary gameplay/3D/FPS acceptance.

systems.title: Session and service composition
systems.summary: Main/F5 instances the existing 3D scene; its shared base controller creates one scene-owned session for rear and battlefield views. BaseSimulation injects the same rear/ledger into domain services. The development opening has four real present unloaders at the south Table service apron.

nodes.label: Build service graph and shared ledger

systems.notes: Configured main.tscn is a root instance of preview.tscn, whose script extends common main.gd. No extra wrapper/controller, autoload or game session is introduced. F6 on either entry also uses 3D. Review scenes may create separate diagnostic sessions. Native input, the complete loop and FPS remain unverified; stages 1/2 await player acceptance.

systems.title: Time, deadlines and settlement
systems.summary: The actual implementation still advances one shared rear time across rear and battlefield services. Live wall-time debt and cooperative route planning feed an event-boundary loop.

nodes.label: Physics callback (at most once per rendered frame in live mode)
Choose nearest service deadline and advance

systems.notes: advance_time queries next_boundary across services, advances work/motion and calls _settle. _settle has a 1000-iteration safety bound; it is not a thousand unconditional passes. Finite event-woken logistics processing is a separate path. Independent domain clocks/timer-only overhaul is NOT completed.

systems.title: Identity, custody, stock and claims
systems.summary: One ledger owns physical people, hulls, stock portions, weapons, holders, ownership, fuel, health and reservations. Services request validated mutations; detached inspections are read models.

nodes.label: Move an actual entity / emit position events

systems.notes: inspect_entity is a query, not the game-loop controller. Many callers share the ledger because goods/people must retain identity across systems. Broad snapshots, narrow queries and mutation APIs coexist; this atlas does not measure their frequency. Explicit activity-owned per-person handling points permit real port arrival without widening global interaction distances. Actual person-held round release emits person_fired for read-only presentation.

systems.title: People: civilian workers and infantry
systems.summary: There are not two independent civilian/infantry entity implementations. The same PERSON identity has assignment, qualification, duty, holder, gear, health, morale and suppression. Different services own its activities.

nodes.label: Shared Person record and Assignment enum

systems.notes: Arrows show possible lifecycle stages, not automatic enlistment. Workers, instructors, crew, passengers and infantry have distinct eligibility/commitment rules. The player manager is a separate ManagerPose/CharacterBody3D, not a free worker identity.

systems.title: Staffing, reporting and priorities
systems.summary: Requested staff, assignment and physical presence are separate. Shared people are rebalanced by duties/priorities and walk/report before contributing work. Development service eligibility includes the apron outside the unchanged construction rectangle. Empty-field people reserve distinct physical service positions through RearWorkPositions; read-only route admission and actual commitment use the same point owner.

nodes.label: Validate actual person and service-strip eligibility
Choose reachable distinct physical work point

systems.notes: One person cannot fill two jobs at once. Newly completed facilities apply their starting request through Construction once; selecting or changing a recipe must not reset deliberate edits. Work points avoid Table/building geometry, preserve person identity and register explicit per-person handling access. Legacy unregistered handling keeps exact colocation. Reservations are not visual offsets or a universal crowd solver. In the empty-field game uncommitted people default to fallback Hauling after workplace/crew quotas. Shared starter-candidate rules preserve once-only automatic workplace demand; safe Reporting completion retries. Actual outbound tasks retain exclusive worker ownership until completion.

systems.title: Storage, hauling and space promises
systems.owner: RearSimulation jobs / actors / stores + ledger claims
systems.summary: Haul requests reserve real source portions and destination capacity. Actor phases represent walking, pickup, carrying and deposit; output space and relocation promises belong to the rear. The default common pool selects its next feasible category in an explicitly confirmed top-first order through existing service owners.
systems.notes: This diagram is the local rear haul path. Strategic manifests, forward trucks and frontline issue have other owners. Construction utility trucks can replace a local long carry leg without creating resources. HaulingPolicy owns preference only. Incoming unloading retains four shared/dedicated slots per berth; ordinary Dispatch retains manifest/route/custody/finite task and real transport/driver. Active safe work is not cancelled by reorder.

systems.title: Purchasing, requisition and inbound deliveries
systems.summary: Receiving owns actual paid resource/worker purchases and physical supplier movement, berth/loading capacity and custody. Development Confirm atomically registers and immediately dispatches one convoy; the final actual handover/departure event reopens ordering while empty egress continues.

nodes.label: Validate and commit one paid convoy
Record actual departure and drain member set

systems.notes: Resources and people are parallel order types, not mandatory sequential steps. Empty-field Supply Table has its own configured receiving arrangement; a Receiving Bay is not required for the first worker purchase. Credit from controlled resource objectives goes to this account. Empty-field workers use reserved actual pickup/drop/arrival points and retain original handling durations/cargo claims. Actual arriving foot positions survive admission instead of collapsing onto the Table centre. Incoming handling accepts idle common haulers through the existing owner; common entries retire after deposit and do not bypass the next category selection. Combined actual jobs retain four slots per berth and25kg carries.

systems.title: Rear building placement, completion and dismantling
systems.summary: ConstructionService owns actual sites, access, partial local-material-supported earned work and incremental consumption. Persistent scene adapters reveal the building; finite scissors/tape/pylons celebrate actual completion without owning capability.
systems.notes: Cancellation and request_dismantle are separate branches with consumed-material/clearance rules. An incomplete/paused/cancelled site does not become a free functional building. Same manager occupation validation is supplied by the 3D view. Empty-field placement validation starts at the shared Table standing-access point, preserving the solid Table and rejecting blocked routes without starting inside its collider. Live cancellation keeps exact site/session/state validation and refreshes actual material loss while builders continue; it is not invalidated by consumption alone. Normal live empty-field startup is1x. Shared licensed prototype exteriors cover buildable kinds; Vehicle Park remains open ground. Presentation listens to keyed owner signals, preserves meshes/colliders across work updates and tears down with site/session lifetime. Follow-up: assigned starved builders may fetch only their own site M11 on foot through existing real claims/carries; one duty/task, no simultaneous construction. Selected menu distinguishes actual haul receipt/carry. Completed exterior retains full-height prepared material, work state does not rebuild unchanged reservations, zero-alpha effect preparation targets measured first-use OpenGL hitch. Smoke1.5s then snip2s, tape release3.5s; actual capability remains immediate. A one-draw startup loading cover prepares actual construction variants in the real camera before input; shared appearance recipe has no gameplay row/stock/physics, and headless entry skips rendering preparation.

systems.title: Construction Office utility truck
systems.summary: A temporary finite Office bundle provides a real T01 hull. The service owns exclusive hauler trips and loading/driving/unloading phases, not a teleporting delivery bonus.
systems.notes: This utility is distinct from Vehicle Works output and ordinary army transport. It retains real cargo and uses the existing clock; rendering is a separate presenter.

systems.title: Shared production and recipe selection
systems.summary: Shared batch lifecycle validates access, operators, physical local inputs and output promise. SelectableProduction adds per-recipe records and confirmed switching of consumed work.

nodes.label: Settle prerequisites and consume local batch

systems.notes: These arrows describe batch lifecycle, not a literal call chain. advance_work is driven by the shared coordinator. Pause retains consumed inputs/work/promise; cancelling a consumed batch loses its unfinished work/inputs.

systems.title: Workshop / F04
systems.summary: Workshop is a configured owner of the shared production lifecycle, not an unrelated crafting engine. Essential R01 manufactures an actual empty E01 rifle; R08 and declared choices share the same facility.
systems.notes: Declared initial-workshop maps explicitly to logical workshop/rear.production. Player-built Workshops use construction.activities[site ID]. The demonstrated 3D interaction used the declared owner; earned full-factory acceptance remains open.

systems.title: Munitions / F05
systems.summary: One exclusive munitions facility selects among ammunition, explosives and shell-chain recipes; ingredients and output are physical stock.

nodes.label: Confirm switch if consumed batch exists

systems.notes: R02, R27, R32 and R33 are choices on the common owner, not four concurrently running batches in one facility. Manufacturing code does not imply that the whole ordinary supply chain has been accepted.

systems.title: Building Materials / F13
systems.summary: A configured fixed production activity consumes local Metal/Wood and produces physical M11 Building Materials for further construction.
systems.notes: The normal opening 500 M11 is declared starting stock; later R26 output is separately manufactured. Self-sustaining ordinary factory completion remains open.

systems.title: Support Workshop / F09
systems.summary: Support recipes reuse the same access, exclusive selection, local-input and physical-output lifecycle.
systems.notes: A support recipe or qualification in a catalogue is not proof of an integrated end-to-end support gameplay loop.

systems.title: Vehicle Works / heavy manufacture
systems.summary: Heavy production extends selectable recipes with actual bay/fleet/parking promises. Completed hulls or heavy objects have canonical IDs; a blocked occupied bay is retained.

nodes.label: Register same hull for rear handling

systems.notes: A produced vehicle is not automatically crewed, fuelled, parked, dispatched or combat-ready. Canonical T01â€“T05 specs are data in vehicle_specs.gd.

systems.title: School, instructors and qualifications
systems.summary: Seats, students and eligible present instructors are real commitments. Elapsed course progress changes qualification on the same Person identity.

nodes.label: Account instructor coverage and course time

systems.notes: Training is elapsed course time with coverage, unlike operator-work manufacturing. Catalogue courses include basic infantry and specialist qualifications; this does not prove every specialist gameplay loop is complete.

systems.title: Rear vehicles, crew, fuel and parking
systems.summary: VehicleActivity owns registered hull activity and refuelling jobs. Ledger owns hull facts, crew station custody, fuel and damage; the renderer does not own these facts.
systems.notes: These are separate vehicle operations, not automatic successive commands. Rear and military fleets retain the same hull ID across accepted handoffs. Different services own different movement activities.

systems.title: Rear â†’ HQ manifests and return
systems.summary: Owns accepted manifests, staging/loading, route, HQ unloading, cancellation and return commitments. Ledger keeps actual cargo/person/hull identities and receipts.
systems.notes: Automatic request fulfilment uses accept_automatic_delivery; retained manual manifests remain distinct. Automatic routine freight does not require a newly added manual Depart action. Ordinary source/staging/loading can use a supplied exclusive common hauler. Real source/staging access precedes pickup; hull port arrival precedes loading. Vehicle/driver/manifest, specialist guns/passengers/HQ and finite task remain existing authorities.

systems.title: HQ receipts, reserve equipment and local issue
systems.summary: HQ issue is a timed local transfer from physically arrived stock to eligible people/vehicles. Receiving at HQ is separate from frontline delivery or use.

nodes.label: Assess and publish genuine rifle need

systems.notes: Person weapon, rounds and vehicle issue are parallel job types. rear_supply_needed is connected to RearLogistics; a shortage signal does not manufacture stock.

systems.title: Automatic factory input and army shipping
systems.summary: Session commits and genuine HQ/frontline need wake finite passes. It requests missing factory hauls and advances automatic delivery requests through existing owners.

nodes.label: Committed session change wakes finite pass
Process one candidate per frame, then idle
Ask activity for actual missing input demand

systems.notes: _process is enabled only while finite candidates remain; there is no idle logistics polling timer. This does not make the entire game event-only: the shared clock and scheduled army reviews still run.

systems.title: Military organization, equipment and readiness
systems.summary: Companies/platoons/squads, demands, crew reports and replacement reports reference real equipped people and attached hulls. Readiness derives from physical facts.
systems.notes: Civilian-to-military duties are ledger assignment/receipt changes, not replacement with a new Infantry object. Autonomous organization is not player RTS soldier-command UI.

systems.title: Military passenger and supply transport
systems.summary: Named trips reserve real people/hull/stations/seats and plan bounded routes. Boarding, travel, interruption and dismount preserve current intent and custody.
systems.notes: Reposition and supply-trip methods are additional guarded paths. This owner is different from rear Dispatch and HQ-to-forward freight.

systems.title: Sight reports, command links and intent
systems.summary: Observations produce side/echelon-specific contacts and delayed reports/orders. Delivered acknowledged intent is consumed by execution; it is not omniscient hidden-target selection.
systems.notes: The ACTIONS catalogue is broader than fully demonstrated autonomous execution. Do not infer every action string has a complete playable path.

systems.title: Squad and vehicle action execution
systems.summary: Delivered intent drives foot movement, cover, combat and resupply decisions. Pending route/decision work is separated from authoritative commits.
systems.notes: Decision scheduling still includes recurring simulation-time reviews. This is not a per-person _process script and is not proof of stable60FPS.

systems.title: Authored operations, resupply and resource decisions
systems.summary: The normal Farmland opening installs scenario-specific policy over reusable organization, orders, execution and transport. Resource proposals and replenishment retain genuine capability/need constraints.
systems.notes: Not a generic campaign AI or procedural-war director. ResourceOperations has a ten-second review interval; some army decision work is scheduled sampling. Availability of these owners does not close ordinary repeated supply acceptance.

systems.title: Rifle squad collection and return journeys
systems.summary: Per-request collection travel chooses feasible walking/transport legs. Execution owns actual foot motions; TroopTransport owns actual vehicle jobs and custody.
systems.notes: Each journey has a cycle/intent identity. It must not revive an obsolete order after resupply. A diagrammed selection path is not a measured optimality or full replenishment result.

systems.title: Frontline person supply issue
systems.summary: After stock physically reaches a declared stop, a named eligible handler picks up, walks and deposits rounds into the actual recipient custody.

nodes.label: Request local issue to actual person

systems.notes: ForwardSupply composes freight and rack-issue subowners. HQ arrival alone does not replenish a person on the battlefield.

systems.title: HQ â†’ forward stop freight and return
systems.summary: Actual military T01, stock portions, handlers, fuel and both route directions are committed to a job. Unloaded forward stock and return are separate phases.
systems.notes: This is a separate movement owner from rear Dispatch. Supply policy observes its jobs and may request later genuine replenishment; no stock is credited merely because a timer was scheduled.

systems.title: Forward vehicle ammunition rack issue
systems.summary: A named local handler moves actual arrived E26 rounds into a permitted vehicle rack, with payload, capacity and exclusivity checks.

nodes.label: Request exact arrived rounds / hull / handler
Validate hull and current station readiness

systems.notes: The current forward-rack path is specifically guarded E26 handling, not a universal arbitrary-vehicle ammo refill framework.

systems.title: Infantry fire, wounds, morale and care
systems.summary: Combat owns fire eligibility, cadence, reload commitments, stress, bleeding/care and squad cohesion. Terrain owns sight/cover and ledger owns actual rounds, injuries and deaths.
systems.notes: Fire, reload, care and cohesion are different branches, not one mandatory sequential chain. Medical care exists inside this service plus field aid facilities; no standalone complete medical logistics system is implied.

systems.title: Mounted weapons, armour and projectiles
systems.summary: T03 MG, T04 autocannon and T05 main/coax have explicit data and actual crew/ammo requirements. Timed aim/reload/projectile work uses existing ledger/world.

nodes.label: Apply actual hull surface and armour damage

systems.notes: Canonical backend mount data is not derived from visible model barrels. Detailed3D T03 art is deferred; T01/T02 visuals are partial/provisional. Do not infer presentation parity from combat implementation. People, heavy guns and structures use their separate existing damage owners.

systems.title: Vehicle destruction, repair and towing
systems.summary: A ledger vehicle-damage signal triggers once-only wreck/occupant consequences. Actual qualified workers/materials and timed coupling/towing own recovery jobs.
systems.notes: Repair and tow are separate branches after damage; neither automatically restores a whole destroyed crew or lost cargo. Not a claim of a fully polished demo recovery UI.

systems.title: Objective capture, control and income
systems.summary: Registered physical places track control, owner, contest, eligible presence and income. Actual uncontested Resource control credits the existing requisition account.
systems.notes: Capture/ownership/income code exists. The recent3D evidence observed initial neutral markers; actual3D capture/contest/owner-transition runtime acceptance remains open.

systems.title: Terrain, footprint, sight and cover queries
systems.summary: Metre-cell/base-region world facts, overlays, obstacles and shields answer terrain support, route footprint, visibility and cover. It is custom domain geometry, not Godot navigation for every entity.
systems.notes: The normal world is authored Farmland4kmÃ—6km. Multiple complete procedural map families and campaign/persistence are not established by terrain catalogue or snapshot methods.

systems.title: Route, hull load and continuation planning
systems.summary: Measured gross load, canonical hull dimensions/turning and terrain/bridge constraints produce route parts. Continuations permit preparation across frames; movement owners commit actual travel.

nodes.label: Read gross actual hull + cargo mass

systems.notes: Pure planning is distinct from boarding, elapsed travel, fuel debit and job admission. The synchronous API and incremental APIs both exist; do not label all routes asynchronous.

systems.title: Field structures, roads and support sites
systems.summary: Projects own local material delivery, eligible engineer work, damage/rebuild, occupancy and completed service use such as lookout, aid, depot, repair and obstacles.
systems.notes: Road/structure capabilities are implemented within this owner/catalogue; they are not independent global building entities or proof of all engineering actions being exposed in the normal3D UI.

systems.title: Bridge construction, crossings and repair
systems.summary: Owns authored/constructed crossing geometry, material/engineer work, traffic queues, load admission, damage and repairs; publishes surfaces to TerrainWorld.
systems.notes: Authored registration and new construction are alternate origins. Crossing damage can retime traffic and cause physical losses; a route preview does not reserve or complete a crossing.

systems.title: Attached demolition charges
systems.summary: D04 is attached to existing field structures/bridges. Local material, qualified engineers, authorization, clearance and fuse/remote-control commitments govern detonation.

nodes.label: Start fuse or guarded remote trigger

systems.notes: Despite ID demo, this is demolition gameplay service; review scenes are classified separately. Fuse and remote are alternate modes, not automatic player access to all hostile devices.

systems.title: Mines, hazards, knowledge and clearance
systems.summary: Actual D01â€“D03 devices, per-side knowledge and timed scan/disarm tasks are distinct from D04 demolition. Ledger movement signals detect physical contacts.
systems.notes: Route hazard knowledge is not omniscient access to every planted device. Placement/knowledge/clearance/contact are branches; main UI and3D visual parity are not established for all.

systems.title: Main menus, rear controls and guidance
systems.summary: The mounted base_demo.gd is the real main management UI despite its filename. Button commands use service owners; retained panels refresh through session commits/time with visibility guards. Combined purchases and staffing use explicit confirmation; model refresh preserves current unconfirmed staffing drafts and model/context replacement invalidates them. Existing-site inspection opens Build controls without acquiring a new blueprint; acquisition retains its separate explicit intent.

nodes.label: Open panel with explicit preview intent
Acquire a new blueprint only by construction intent

systems.notes: Hidden UI intentionally skips expensive refresh. This matters to selection:3D Workshop opens management before resolving current facility metadata. Existing scroll-heavy layout remains; generated diagrams do not establish enjoyable UI acceptance. Hauling has a composed inline disclosure with native grip drag/insertion line and keyboard/button fallback. Draft survives live status refresh; Confirm delegates once to Rear; central menu close discards unconfirmed changes.

systems.title: Battlefield read models and 2D inspection
systems.summary: Read models select permitted own units/observed contacts and objective facts. Inspection and supply-stage feedback use actual identities with existing information restrictions. Existing3D observation now has ID-keyed provisional friendly T03 and T04 hulls and distinct permitted report cues, shared picking/inspection and canonical deadline-driven report expiry. No duplicate simulation, hidden enemy bodies or approved-art/FPS claim.

systems.notes: Presentation reads do not issue military orders or grant knowledge. Snapshot/marker APIs are query layers, not independent simulation state owners.

systems.summary: Main/F5 reuses this 3D scene around the same manager/session, actual site/Table E interactions, first/third-person views and overhead grid construction. Supplier visuals subscribe to Receiving state and keyed ledger movement; they do not own purchases or vehicle motion. Artist-supplied worker/soldier models replace provisional manager duplicates; CharacterVisual binds actual state to imported in-place clips and attachments.

Purchase and placement still use explicit draft/commit commands and their existing owners. Source structure and scoped evidence do not establish player acceptance, full 3D migration or FPS.

systems.owner: FieldPersons / FieldT01Trucks / FieldObjectives + cached cue overlays
systems.summary: Scene-owned presenters reconcile permitted rows; keyed changes update actual poses and cached screen anchors. Cue projection/picking is separate from domain combat.
systems.notes: People, hulls and objectives are parallel presenters. Existing field_t01 paths support exactly T01/T02; their name is historical. T02 exterior is provisional commercial art, T03 detailed exterior deferred, objective transition runtime open. People now retain Artist-supplied skeletons and clips, with detailed animation gated by visibility and zoom. systems.summary: The manager has one persistent foot pose with heading; first/third cameras are views of it. The manager is not a PERSON staff member or camera-position proxy.

systems.notes: Switching perspective does not create free workers. Full grounded vehicle contact/displacement/hold integration is deferred; current query-only truck shapes must not be called completed manager collision integration.

systems.title: Authored world, opening armies and normal rear start
systems.summary: Scenario creation composes the4kmÃ—6km world, declared forces/objectives/stops and authored operation policy. Normal empty-field creation is distinct from legacy prebuilt diagnostic sessions.

nodes.label: Create shared session and declared world

systems.notes: The normal opening is one manager,2500REQ,500M11,Supply Table and no free hired workers/workshops. Main debug/review constructors have distinct arrangements. No persistent campaign/save system or complete multi-family procedural generator is established here.

systems.title: Explicit prototype debug actions
systems.summary: The menu dispatches explicit cheats against the current supplied model and marks debug_used. These bypasses are distinct from ordinary production, purchase and delivery.
systems.notes: The last three nodes are alternate debug branches. They must not be used to claim earned ordinary-loop acceptance.

systems.title: Function-call logging and retained performance tooling
systems.summary: Instrumentation counts instrumented entries and optionally unique caller stacks per real second. It is a diagnostic observer, not every possible function automatically instrumented or tested.
systems.notes: Counter reports are not a measured cost ranking. GDUnit/test sources and menu performance harness remain retained; current policy does not run old suites or claim every button/function is tested. No engine or regression was run for this atlas.

systems.title: Optional review scenes, fixtures and probes
systems.summary: The repo retains subsystem demos/fixtures, a synthetic full-size probe and overhead evaluation. Many are available from optional Diagnostics; they are not evidence of ordinary gameplay completion.
systems.notes: base_demo is deliberately NOT classified here: it is mounted main UI. Optional scenes may instantiate independent simulations. Test files are listed under their subsystem in the source inventory, with retained-test classification; no test suite was executed.

systems.title: Worker and soldier model animation
systems.summary: Actual activity/position facts select imported Artist clips. Game services retain world motion, stock custody, labour and shots. Bone-local cargo and a separate equipped rifle use the exported attachment matrices. Existing personal-weapon reload facts drive the seventh soldier clip at the actual reload duration; imported vertex palettes are explicitly enabled.

Soldier wounded_idle is mapped explicitly. Source/Artist QA and narrow integration evidence do not establish every action, universal avoidance, native input or FPS.
